channel.title: Food Safety Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Food Safety Magazine (food-safety.com)

item.title: Preventive Maintenance: A Complex Prerequisite Program
item.description: Preventive maintenance, which involves a great deal of documentation and recordkeeping, can be considered as the most complex and detailed of the essential prerequisite programs.

item.title: New UK PFAS Action Plan Addresses ‘Forever Chemicals’ in Food
item.description: The UK Government’s PFAS Plan addresses human dietary exposure and food and water contamination, environmental monitoring, potentially restricting PFAS uses, and other actions.

item.title: FAO/WHO Experts Publish Report on Control Measures for Foodborne Viruses of Concern
item.description: The FAO/WHO Joint Expert Meeting on Microbiological Risk Assessment (JEMRA) has published a report on prevention and intervention measures for foodborne virus–commodity pairs of concern.

item.title: Food Safety Spending Cuts Associated with Fewer Hygiene Interventions by England Authorities, Study Shows
item.description: Although food safety spending cuts were associated with local authority staffing reductions and decreases in the number of official food hygiene interventions, industry compliance was not negatively affected.

item.title: NASDA’s 2026 Policy Priorities Focus on Pesticides, Animal Diseases, and Farm Bill Food Safety
item.description: The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture (NASDA) has set its federal policy priorities for 2026. Food safety-related issues are central to NASDA's 2026 advocacy work for the Farm Bill, animal diseases and traceability, and pesticides

item.title: Report Raises Concerns About U.S. Food Recall Timeliness, Transparency in 2025
item.description: The U.S. Public Interest Research Group (PIRG) Education Fund’s newly published Food for Thought report outlines food recalls and foodborne illness outbreak investigations that occurred in 2025 and provides recommendations for improving the U.S. food recall system.

item.title: FDA to Begin Testing Infant Formula Products, Ingredients for C. botulinum
item.description: Following the ByHeart botulism outbreak, FDA intends to begin testing infant formula products and ingredients for Clostridium botulinum to help determine whether contamination by the pathogen is a “foreseeable hazard that companies could test for.”

item.title: New Jersey Passes Ban on PFAS in Food Packaging
item.description: New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy has signed into law the Protecting Against Forever Chemicals Act which prohibits statewide the manufacture and sale of certain consumer goods that contain intentionally added per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

item.title: FAO/WHO Call for Experts to Support Microbiological Risk Assessment for Infant Formula
item.description: In the wake of a high-profile safety incidents involving powdered infant formula, FAO/WHO have issued a call for experts and data to support JEMRA in conducting a risk assessment that will help the Codex Committee on Food Hygiene update the Codex Alimentarius standards for powdered formula.

item.title: FDA Allows Foods with ‘Natural’ Food Dyes to Claim ‘No Artificial Colors’
item.description: As part of its efforts to encourage industry to phase out the use of petroleum-based synthetic food dyes, FDA is expanding the allowed uses of the label claim “no artificial colors” on food products and has approved a new naturally derived colorant for food.
